effect: The cell has divided into two pluripotent daughters with complete nuclear genomes, completing the goal; their later specialization can involve different patterns of gene expression.
reaction: The final picture ties nuclear division and separation of the cell body together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing the copied genome together with the spindle was most worthwhile: the result distinguishes separating sister chromatids from dividing the whole cell.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making membrane vesicles was less satisfying because their formation was not explained, and it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The replication result emphasized that the whole nuclear genome is copied, including noncoding DNA, rather than only protein-coding material.

arbitrary.text: Combining phospholipids and proteins to make vesicles had a clear growth purpose, but the connection to vesicle formation was not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the chapter connected genome copying, chromosome separation and cell division in a useful sequence, and the final reference to gene expression suggests a worthwhile next topic.
